rejected.title: Writing about personal journeys
card: Personal journeys is a framework of ideas for creating texts. It explores change, growth and identity, and the paths people travel.
A journey can be literal, such as moving to a new country or walking a long trail. It can also be inner, such as learning to trust someone or letting go of a goal.
A strong piece shows a change in the person. The writer needs a starting point, something that tests the character, and a new understanding or state at the end.
The change can be small, mixed or unfinished. A character may grow, but also lose something, or end with questions still open.
rejected.remember: A personal journey text is about change in a person, whether the path is literal or inner.

a.q: Which story idea is most clearly built around the personal journeys framework?
opts: A girl dreads a race and slowly gains self-belief
A boy takes a long train trip and stays just the same
A woman describes her town's market in close detail
A man gives a speech asking the council to close a road
a.why: The girl who dreads the race changes: she starts in doubt, is tested, and ends with self-belief. The train trip is a literal path, but the boy stays the same, so it shows no change in the person.
a.clue: Look for a person who is changed by what happens.

b.q: Priya plans a story about a girl who walks the same road to school each day. Nothing in the girl changes, but the weather does. What is the main problem with this plan for a personal journeys piece?
opts: The girl shows no change or growth through the walk
The road is a literal path, so it cannot be a journey
The story has no argument about a school policy
The weather is too small a detail to use in a story
b.why: A strong personal journeys piece shows a change in the person, and here the girl stays the same. The literal path is not the problem, because a journey can be literal. A change in the weather is not a change in the character.
b.clue: A journey can be literal. Who in the story should change?

a.q: Which piece of writing is most clearly built around the personal journeys framework?
opts: A teenager who dreads a race slowly gains self-belief
A report listing the opening hours of a regional train line
A speech arguing that a council should close a local road
A description of a street market at noon, with no one in focus
a.why: The first piece follows a person who changes, which is the core of the framework. The train report is about travel, but it shows no change in a person, so a literal route alone is not enough.
a.clue: Look for a person who is changed by what happens.
